title: Mist Over the Garden Pond
technique: Left hand moves in parallel chord shapes, keeping the same voicing as the harmony shifts. Keep the tempo relaxed and the melody singing; accuracy matters more than speed.
body: Mist Over the Garden Pond is a complete impressionist piano song in C major, in 4/4 time at 72 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is hazy color and atmosphere over strict form. The A sections move through tonic, supertonic, submediant, dominant color, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original realization built on a public-domain impressionist framework: whole-tone, pentatonic and modal color with parallel chord movement. It is not attributed to any composer and it is not a copy of any existing impressionist work. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: parallel chord shapes in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Arabesque in Soft Green
technique: Left hand plays a low bass note answered by mid-range chord blocks. Keep the tempo relaxed and the melody singing; accuracy matters more than speed.
body: Arabesque in Soft Green is a complete impressionist piano song in F major, in 4/4 time at 66 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is hazy color and atmosphere over strict form. The A sections move through tonic, supertonic, submediant, dominant color, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original realization built on a public-domain impressionist framework: whole-tone, pentatonic and modal color with parallel chord movement. It is not attributed to any composer and it is not a copy of any existing impressionist work. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: bass note plus chord blocks in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Evening Bells in the Valley
technique: Left hand arpeggiates each chord, rolling the tones evenly across the bar. Keep the tempo relaxed and the melody singing; accuracy matters more than speed.
body: Evening Bells in the Valley is a complete impressionist piano song in Bb major, in 4/4 time at 72 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is hazy color and atmosphere over strict form. The A sections move through tonic, supertonic, submediant, dominant color, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original realization built on a public-domain impressionist framework: whole-tone, pentatonic and modal color with parallel chord movement. It is not attributed to any composer and it is not a copy of any existing impressionist work. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: arpeggiated chords in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: The Quiet Fountain Court
technique: Left hand plays a low bass note answered by mid-range chord blocks. Keep the tempo relaxed and the melody singing; accuracy matters more than speed.
body: The Quiet Fountain Court is a complete impressionist piano song in Eb major, in 3/4 time at 84 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is hazy color and atmosphere over strict form. The A sections move through tonic, supertonic, submediant, dominant color, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original realization built on a public-domain impressionist framework: whole-tone, pentatonic and modal color with parallel chord movement. It is not attributed to any composer and it is not a copy of any existing impressionist work. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: bass note plus chord blocks in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Reflections in a Rain Pool
technique: Left hand arpeggiates each chord, rolling the tones evenly across the bar. Shape the phrasing in two-bar breaths and let the syncopation sit inside the beat, never ahead of it.
body: Reflections in a Rain Pool is a complete impressionist piano song in E major, in 3/4 time at 96 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-B-A-B form across 4 sections. Its mood is hazy color and atmosphere over strict form. The A sections move through tonic, supertonic, submediant, dominant color, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original realization built on a public-domain impressionist framework: whole-tone, pentatonic and modal color with parallel chord movement. It is not attributed to any composer and it is not a copy of any existing impressionist work. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: arpeggiated chords in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: The Distant Shepherd's Pipe
technique: Left hand plays a low bass note answered by mid-range chord blocks. Shape the phrasing in two-bar breaths and let the syncopation sit inside the beat, never ahead of it.
body: The Distant Shepherd's Pipe is a complete impressionist piano song in C major, in 4/4 time at 72 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is hazy color and atmosphere over strict form. The A sections move through tonic, supertonic, submediant, dominant color, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original realization built on a public-domain impressionist framework: whole-tone, pentatonic and modal color with parallel chord movement. It is not attributed to any composer and it is not a copy of any existing impressionist work. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: bass note plus chord blocks in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Waves on a Sheltered Shore
technique: Left hand plays a low bass note answered by mid-range chord blocks. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: Waves on a Sheltered Shore is a complete impressionist piano song in D major, in 3/4 time at 96 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-B-A-B form across 4 sections. Its mood is hazy color and atmosphere over strict form. The A sections move through tonic, supertonic, submediant, dominant color, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original realization built on a public-domain impressionist framework: whole-tone, pentatonic and modal color with parallel chord movement. It is not attributed to any composer and it is not a copy of any existing impressionist work. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: bass note plus chord blocks in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: The Floating Lantern Path
technique: Left hand moves in parallel chord shapes, keeping the same voicing as the harmony shifts. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: The Floating Lantern Path is a complete impressionist piano song in Bb major, in 4/4 time at 72 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is hazy color and atmosphere over strict form. The A sections move through tonic, supertonic, submediant, dominant color, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original realization built on a public-domain impressionist framework: whole-tone, pentatonic and modal color with parallel chord movement. It is not attributed to any composer and it is not a copy of any existing impressionist work. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: parallel chord shapes in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Wind Through the Reeds
technique: Left hand arpeggiates each chord, rolling the tones evenly across the bar. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: Wind Through the Reeds is a complete impressionist piano song in Eb major, in 3/4 time at 84 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is hazy color and atmosphere over strict form. The A sections move through tonic, supertonic, submediant, dominant color, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original realization built on a public-domain impressionist framework: whole-tone, pentatonic and modal color with parallel chord movement. It is not attributed to any composer and it is not a copy of any existing impressionist work. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: arpeggiated chords in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: First Snow on the Temple Steps
technique: Left hand moves in parallel chord shapes, keeping the same voicing as the harmony shifts. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: First Snow on the Temple Steps is a complete impressionist piano song in E major, in 3/4 time at 96 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-B-A-B form across 4 sections. Its mood is hazy color and atmosphere over strict form. The A sections move through tonic, supertonic, submediant, dominant color, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is an original realization built on a public-domain impressionist framework: whole-tone, pentatonic and modal color with parallel chord movement. It is not attributed to any composer and it is not a copy of any existing impressionist work. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: parallel chord shapes in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.
